clue.text: Emigre after surgery gets note for course of treatment

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges, so the word before it comes out in a new order

explanation.surface: An émigré who has had an operation is put on a recovery plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed programme of diet, exercise or medication, so a planned course of treatment.

clue.text: Tranquil end to summer with flutes playing

indicators.note: end to picks the final letter of the word that follows
playing means the letters are in play, mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A calm close to summer, with flute music in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means calm and soothing, conducive to rest, so peaceful or quiet.

clue.text: Summing up, say, I have condensed part of speech

parts.note: summing, the -ing verb form used as a noun, is an example of a gerund
I have shortened gives the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A grammarian sums up, confessing to having trimmed some speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks summing as an example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerundive is a Latin verbal adjective, one of the word classes in grammar.

clue.text: Obsession in Asian capital to ban liberal

indicators.note: banning shuts something out, so the letter is removed from the city

parts.note: Manila is the capital of the Philippines

explanation.surface: A fixation in an Asian city on outlawing liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is an excessive enthusiasm or craze, a compulsive fixation.

clue.text: Reportedly, figures that are dubbed secure in club?

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word rather than see it spelt

parts.note: those dubbed with a sword are knighted, so knights
to pot is to win or bag something, as in potting a prize

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that knighted figures shelter in a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is spoken: KNIGHTS heard as NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub; the question mark flags club in its entertainment sense rather than a society.

clue.text: Excitement for a rocketeer — or annoyance for a hiker?

definitions.meaning: the moment a rocket leaves the launch pad, the thrilling high point for anyone launching rockets
a hitchhiker is annoyed when an offered ride is cancelled, read as two words

explanation.surface: One activity's thrill is another's frustration: rockets versus roadside travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as two words: a hitchhiker's lift being off, i.e. the ride is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Launch is the climax of rocketry, while a withdrawn ride strands a hitchhiker; both senses fit the phrase.

clue.text: Purple colour arising in topical illustration

indicators.note: arising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shade of mauve emerges in a picture of current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'arising' reads upward: CALIL in topiCAL ILlustration, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale mauve shade named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Man's possessive in country given commercial concession

indicators.note: in places the possessive inside the country

parts.note: France, the European nation
his is the possessive pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man's acquisitiveness abroad wins him a business licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence granted to trade under a company's name, a commercial right or concession.

clue.text: Head provides view dismissing Greek character

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an opinion is one's view
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A leader gives an opinion while firing a Greek figure.
explanation.walkthrough: ONION is old slang for the head, as in 'off your onion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is British slang for the head, as in the phrase 'off one's onion' meaning crazy.

clue.text: Revive request for quiet in unconstrained start to negotiations

indicators.note: in places the hush inside the word for unconstrained

parts.note: free means unrestricted
sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Calls for hush rejuvenate the opening of free-flowing talks.
explanation.definitionFit: To freshen is to make something fresh again, to refresh or revive it.

clue.text: Gentleman given two directions for warning device

parts.note: Sir is the title or polite address for a gentleman
E and N are the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: A gentleman is handed a couple of bearings to steer by a warning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a device sounding a loud wailing alarm, as on ambulances or air-raid warnings.

clue.text: Stir leading group on island beset by strong wind

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it, so the strong wind goes around the rest

parts.note: a gale is a very strong wind
the van is the vanguard, the group at the front

explanation.surface: A storm-lashed island's foremost party is roused into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading group' is the van, as in vanguard, not a band's frontmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise is to shock or rouse someone into action, so to stir them.

clue.text: Cool time with a good man in charge — that's excellent

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it with moving air
ST, saint, is the crossword's stock good man

explanation.surface: A laid-back period with a decent fellow at the helm is praised as superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' is a verb here, not slang for great.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is an informal superlative meaning wonderful or superb, a synonym of excellent.

clue.text: Military supremo with hard or easy thing to do

parts.note: C-in-C, Commander-in-Chief, is the top military officer
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A commanding general weighs a tough task against an easy one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is an informal term for something certain or very simple to accomplish.

clue.text: The French defend backward port and river

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so the French article goes around the port

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: backward says the port's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is often just Rio

explanation.surface: French forces hold a harbour town and a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, flowing to the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire.

clue.text: Complete university competition after injection of new stamina

parts.note: to end something is to complete it

indicators.note: the race has had the letter for new injected into it

parts.note: a race is a contest

explanation.surface: A finished varsity contest, after a fresh dose, leaves competitors with staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injection of' puts N into RACE as RA...CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going under strain, which is what stamina means.

clue.text: Exotic fruit in small measure consumed by individual

indicators.note: being consumed means being taken inside, so the measure goes within the individual

parts.note: a person is an individual
1 mm, one millimetre, is a tiny length; the 1 is written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone eats a little portion of a foreign fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small measure' is 1 mm with the digit swapped for the Roman I, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange tropical-looking fruit of the Diospyros tree, often sold as sharon fruit.

clue.text: Older mole in training offering an inspiration for aspirants?

indicators.note: training reshapes and drills, so these letters are put through new formations

explanation.surface: A veteran spy in training sets an example to newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' is a spy, and 'in training' rearranges OLDER MOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others look up to and copy, an exemplar.

clue.text: One in official writing admitting qualm

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the writing

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is a formal written document
I is the Roman numeral one
giving, as in conceding a point, means admitting it

explanation.surface: Someone admits a doubt in a formal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension, like a qualm.

clue.text: Note a lad busy around college with liking for narrative

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
a busy scene is full of bustle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boy at a college jots a message while busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anecdotal relies on stories and personal accounts, showing a fondness for telling tales.

clue.text: Publicises question for activity needing aces?

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
how is a question word

explanation.surface: Someone broadcasts a query about a pursuit requiring experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aces' are star pilots, not playing cards or tennis serves.
explanation.definitionFit: An air show is a display of aerobatic flying, which needs expert pilots, called aces.

clue.text: Some take a selfie as support for artist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people photograph themselves using a painter's stand as a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden stand that holds a painter's canvas, a prop for the artist's work.

clue.text: Liquid leaking in connection

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Fluid is seeping out of a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkage is a system of links or a joining between things, a connection.

clue.text: Addition to a legal document for a cyclist?

definitions.meaning: a clause tacked on to a bill, contract or verdict
someone who sits on and pedals a bicycle

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is both an appended clause in law and a person riding a bike or horse.

clue.text: French aristocrat appreciated revolutionary old coin

parts.note: duc is French for duke

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ta is a British word of thanks, said when something is appreciated

explanation.surface: A French nobleman, valued by revolutionaries, holds an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe from medieval times.

clue.text: Love to be in camp in ground working for friend

indicators.note: the love letter is to be placed inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms inside a campsite on the operational ground, for a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges CAMP IN to CMPANI; 'to be in' places O after the C, then ON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion is someone you spend time with, a comrade or friend.

clue.text: Aquatic rodent is evasive with place cut off

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, so evasive

indicators.note: cut off says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A water creature is shy, its home isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water-dwelling rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: A trip at sea heading north gets assumed designation

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: a sail is a voyage on a boat

explanation.surface: A voyage northwards under a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false name someone adopts, an assumed identity.

clue.text: Journalist observed around November characterising old material?

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to eye something is to watch it, so eyed means observed

explanation.surface: A reporter was seen near November recycling stale stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed describes phrases or ideas overused to the point of staleness, as worn-out material is.

clue.text: Trade in capital kept back in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: in places the trade word inside the reversed capital
kept back says the word for capital is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, as capital does, written AI
biz is slang for business or trade

explanation.surface: Commerce in a city held in reserve within a sunny holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is the old adjective meaning excellent, A1, here AI; 'kept back' makes IA, and BIZ goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean, a Spanish party destination.

clue.text: Measure of power shown by French water painter

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A power rating shown on a Gallic water heater, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was an 18th-century French artist known for his fête galante scenes.

clue.text: Almost final time to digest northern Italian food

indicators.note: almost says the word for final loses its last letter

parts.note: the last thing is the final one

indicators.note: digesting takes something inside, so the time word swallows the next letter

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Nearly the last moment to digest a meal of northern Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern' looks attached to 'Italian food' but gives N, which 'to digest' puts inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is the Italian dish of layered flat pasta sheets with sauce and cheese.
